tiers: Default: not allowed unless instructor permits

documents.summary: The Faculty Senate page gives optional syllabus statements. Its default bars AI that creates academic content without instructor permission, and it adds four sample permissive and restrictive statements that instructors can adopt, including one for coding help.
documents.stance_why: The page sets a default ("not allowed unless permission is given by an instructor") but also offers sample permissive and restrictive templates for instructors to choose from, so under the codebook rule on templates it is coded delegates with the tiers listed.

units.why: The page says the syllabus statements are optional but verbatim if used; that is a rule on how instructors adopt the Senate text. No type covers optional-but-verbatim adoption, so UNCOVERED.

units.uncovered_note: Senate-approved syllabus statements are optional, but if adopted must be used word for word.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence FAQ (student resources)
documents.summary: The Provost's academic integrity FAQ defines generative AI and says students may use it only when instructors allow, with rules varying by program, course and assignment. It covers citation, record-keeping, Grammarly, and why the university cares, and tells students to ask when unsure.
documents.stance_why: The FAQ says "Students can only use artificial intelligence tools when allowed by instructors" and that unauthorized use is prohibited by the integrity policy, so the default is ban-unless-permitted (restrict), even though the permission itself is left to instructors.

units.why: The FAQ defines generative AI as tools "that can draft or substantively edit academic work for a user", which sets the policy's scope (P61).
